rules.rule:
QNSC workflow conventions, on top of the built-in GitHub Actions rules.

## Pinning
- Third-party actions are pinned by 40-character commit SHA with the version in a trailing
  comment. A tag can be moved; a SHA cannot. Reusable workflow calls within this organisation use
  `@v1` by convention — that distinction is deliberate, so do not flag it.

## A required check must be able to report
- A check named in branch protection that never reports does not fail: it blocks every merge
  forever. Flag a rename of a job or a `name:` that a ruleset requires, and flag converting an
  action call into a reusable workflow call, which changes the reported check name to
  `<caller>/<called>`.

## Secrets and permissions
- `permissions` must be least-privilege at the job, not inherited broadly.
- Flag a secret echoed, written to an output, or interpolated into a `run:` line where an `env:`
  entry would keep it out of the command.
- Flag `pull_request_target` combined with a checkout of the head ref; that runs untrusted code
  with write access.

## Reality of the runner
- Flag a step that assumes a tool exists without installing or checking it.
- Flag a long-running step with no timeout.
- Flag a build step that mutates a tracked file: it leaves a dirty tree that rides along in the
  next commit.
